clue.text: Secret Scottish group almost all doomed

parts.note: a clan is a Scottish family group

indicators.note: almost all of the word means it loses its final letter

parts.note: doomed means destined, fated to a bad end

explanation.surface: A hidden Highland family is nearly all fated for ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost all' cuts the last letter from DESTINED, leaving DESTINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clandestine is kept covert, done in secrecy.

clue.text: Go on to cannabis? That's crazy

parts.note: to have a crack is to have a go
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Moving on to cannabis is said to be madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on to' joins the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot idea is eccentric or mad.

clue.text: An expert in charge but it's chaotic

parts.note: taken as written
arch means chief or masterly, as in an arch-exponent

explanation.surface: A capable person is in command, yet everything is in disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchic means lawless and disordered.

clue.text: Put clothes on and bandage

definitions.meaning: to apply a covering to a wound

explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers clothing a person and covering a wound.

clue.text: Come up with expert on breaking waves

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the expert below the waves

parts.note: surf is waves breaking on a shore
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A skilled surfer arrives with an expert on the breakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To surface is to rise to the top of water, emerge.

clue.text: Drive off: time's up

indicators.note: off means the letters are out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written, with its S

explanation.surface: A driver leaves because the time is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges TIMESUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the force or momentum that drives something forward.

clue.text: Mine is invested in landed property mostly — a French boozer

indicators.note: invested here means placed inside, so the mine goes within the other piece
mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an estate is landed property
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has put money into a country estate — and a French bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final E of the property; 'is invested in' wraps that shortened word around the mine, and the surface's money sense of invested misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French café selling drinks, i.e. a bar or pub.

clue.text: Blimey, it's a short string!

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: a cord is a length of string

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at how little string is left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the final D of CORD. COR is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'blimey'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang exclamations of astonishment, interchangeable in speech.

clue.text: Definitely settle for lover's embrace

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to seal a deal and a close embrace.

clue.text: Scruffy person moves garbage about without energy

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned around and rearranged
without means the following letter is removed

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An untidy person shifts rubbish around without much effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes E from GARBAGE; 'about' rearranges GARBAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragbag is, colloquially, a slovenly or scruffily dressed person.

clue.text: Ottoman leader takes note it's a precious stone

parts.note: an aga was a commander or chief in the Ottoman Empire
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A Turkish chief receives a message about a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded semiprecious form of chalcedony, used as a gemstone.

clue.text: Again pocketing nurseryman's job as plants grow

parts.note: the prefix re- means again
in snooker, pocketing a ball is potting it

explanation.surface: A gardener describes once more taking in plants as they get bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pocketing' looks like a container signal but is just the snooker sense of potting.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener moves growing plants into larger containers, the task named here.

clue.text: Stops using bitter to get engine going

parts.note: to kick a habit is to stop using something
tart means sour or bitter in taste

explanation.surface: Someone gives up their pint of bitter in order to start the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' suggests the beer, but it is the adjective, giving TART.
explanation.definitionFit: A kick-start fires up a motorbike engine with a downward push of the foot.

clue.text: Doctor has tea and strong coffee

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A physician drinks both tea and a powerful coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine, strongly flavoured coffee named after the Yemeni port.

clue.text: Opening force is deployed to cover two separated islands

indicators.note: deployed troops are rearranged into position, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island; two of them give a pair of I's, which end up apart

explanation.surface: Troops are sent out to guard a pair of distant islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is deployed' rearranges FORCE with the two I's; 'separated' hints that the I's are not side by side in the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is a hole or aperture, such as a mouth or vent.

clue.text: In it, a beer that's brewed to be drunk

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone drops something into a freshly made beer before drinking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's brewed' rearranges INITABEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Inebriate as an adjective means intoxicated.

clue.text: All there inside know he has a nervous disposition

indicators.note: inside means the letters are found within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A speaker insists that a man is mentally fine despite his anxious temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' points to the letters in 'haS A NErvous'; 'know he' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone 'all there' is of sound mind, an idiom for mental soundness.

clue.text: Support the team that's bottom

parts.note: to back is to support
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A fan backs the side that is last in the league.
explanation.definitionFit: The backside is the buttocks, one's rear.

clue.text: Gut feeling could get in the way in court

parts.note: taken as written
ST is short for street, a way
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hunch could prove an obstacle in a legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: Instinct is an intuitive, unreasoned sense.

clue.text: Put me on ship where servicemen eat

parts.note: taken as written
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be posted aboard a vessel's dining hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is the dining hall where members of the armed forces take meals.

clue.text: Boat's fuel comes from what's beneath the earth's surface

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a boat; the 's gives the S
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: A submarine's fuel is drawn from underground.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsoil is the layer lying under the topsoil.

clue.text: Get on board: there's a small space in front of coach

indicators.note: in front of places the space before the coach in the answer

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space, half an em
a coach is a railway carriage, so a train

explanation.surface: Passengers are told to board, with a gap before the railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a typesetting measure of space, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrain is to board a train, especially of troops.

clue.text: Final destination for goods ensured new order

indicators.note: a new order means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh purchase order makes sure the products arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new order' rearranges ENSURED.
explanation.definitionFit: The end user is the consumer at whom a product is ultimately aimed.

clue.text: Head off from port for a shady spot

indicators.note: head off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a harbour is a port

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the harbour to find a shaded place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' removes the H from HARBOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbour is a bower shaded by trees or climbing plants.

clue.text: It's one desire that's excessive, OK?

parts.note: a means one
greed is excessive desire

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether their overindulgence is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed is used as an exclamation of assent, like 'all right'.

clue.text: Acknowledgement of message for notorious lodger

definitions.meaning: in radio procedure, this word means 'message received'
'the lodger' of British comic tradition is a rhyming name for a lodger who seduces the landlady

explanation.surface: A radio operator confirms a signal about a disreputable tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roger the Lodger' is a British comic stock figure, a lodger with designs on the landlady.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio users say this name to mean received; the rhyming stock character is the notorious tenant.

clue.text: Sleep with sailor and in France put on something over nightdress

parts.note: bed stands for sleep, as in 'time for bed'
jack, as in jack tar, is a sailor
et is the French for and

explanation.surface: A risqué tale of sleeping with a sailor and dressing up in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' is surface padding, suggesting dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed jacket is a short garment worn over nightwear while sitting up in bed.

clue.text: Quickly step behind animal's head

indicators.note: in a down clue, behind places the step after the other piece
the head of the word is its first letter

parts.note: a pace is a step

explanation.surface: Someone moves quickly, stepping behind an animal's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace means swiftly or rapidly.

clue.text: They work producing music and drama (wrong sort)

parts.note: opera combines music and drama

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of the following word are put out of order

explanation.surface: Some people complain that a production combining music and drama is of the wrong kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges SORT into TORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Operators are people who run machines, i.e. workers.

clue.text: Arrange in a line; in a line, you hear!

indicators.note: you hear means the word sounds like the phrase before it

parts.note: taken as written, the phrase spoken

explanation.surface: Someone stresses arranging things in a row, repeating themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you hear' signals that 'a line' spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To align is to put things into a straight row.

clue.text: Stick nothing in the way

indicators.note: in means the zero goes inside the abbreviation for road

parts.note: RD is short for road, a way
O resembles zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Something long and thin is lying in the path.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is a slender pole or stick.

clue.text: Big Guys Hospital department encloses them with blown-up photo

indicators.note: encloses means the department's letters surround the other piece

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
big guys are large men

explanation.surface: Bulky men at Guy's Hospital crowd into a department with a big photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy's is a London hospital, so the capital G misleads. 'them' refers back to the big guys.
explanation.definitionFit: An enlargement is a print made bigger than the original negative.
